standards.description: Teach students to apply the integration by parts formula and use the tabular method for repeated applications to evaluate products of functions.
standards.ccssText: Apply integration by parts using the formula integral(u dv) = uv - integral(v du); select u and dv strategically using the LIATE guideline; use the tabular method for repeated applications; recognize when to reapply integration by parts or solve for the integral algebraically.

standards.description: Help students evaluate integrals involving powers of trigonometric functions and apply trigonometric substitution for integrals containing radical expressions.
standards.ccssText: Evaluate integrals of the form integral(sin^m x cos^n x dx) and integral(tan^m x sec^n x dx) using reduction identities; apply trigonometric substitutions x = a sin(theta), x = a tan(theta), or x = a sec(theta) to eliminate radicals of the form sqrt(a^2 - x^2), sqrt(a^2 + x^2), and sqrt(x^2 - a^2).

standards.description: Guide students to decompose rational functions into partial fractions and integrate each component, covering distinct linear, repeated linear, and irreducible quadratic factors.
standards.ccssText: Decompose proper rational functions into partial fractions over distinct linear, repeated linear, and irreducible quadratic factors; determine unknown coefficients by comparing numerators or substituting values; integrate each partial fraction component.

standards.description: Teach students to evaluate improper integrals with infinite limits or discontinuous integrands using limits, and determine convergence or divergence.
standards.ccssText: Evaluate improper integrals with infinite limits of integration or discontinuous integrands by replacing problematic bounds with a variable and taking a limit; classify as convergent or divergent; apply comparison to determine convergence without evaluating.

standards.description: Guide students to identify and solve separable first-order differential equations by separating variables and integrating both sides.
standards.ccssText: Identify separable first-order differential equations; separate variables by writing f(y) dy = g(x) dx; integrate both sides; apply initial conditions to find particular solutions; verify solutions by substitution.

standards.description: Help students construct and interpret slope fields for first-order differential equations and sketch solution curves through given initial points.
standards.ccssText: Construct a slope field for a differential equation dy/dx = f(x, y) by computing and plotting slopes at a grid of points; sketch plausible solution curves through specified points; interpret slope fields qualitatively without solving the equation.

standards.description: Teach students to apply Euler's Method step by step to approximate the solution to an initial value problem numerically.
standards.ccssText: Apply Euler's Method to approximate solutions to initial value problems using the iterative formula y_(n+1) = y_n + f(x_n, y_n) * delta x; understand that smaller step sizes yield more accurate approximations; compute several iterations by hand and interpret the results.

standards.description: Help students set up and solve differential equations for exponential and logistic growth and decay models and interpret the parameters in context.
standards.ccssText: Set up and solve dP/dt = kP to obtain exponential growth/decay P(t) = P0 e^(kt); set up and solve the logistic equation dP/dt = kP(1 - P/M) and interpret carrying capacity M; apply to population, radioactive decay, Newton's law of cooling, and related contexts.

standards.description: Help students find first and second derivatives for parametric curves and compute arc length using the parametric arc length formula.
standards.ccssText: Find dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt) for parametric curves; find d^2y/dx^2 using the chain rule; compute arc length using L = integral(sqrt((dx/dt)^2 + (dy/dt)^2) dt); find areas under parametric curves.

standards.description: Guide students to convert between polar and rectangular coordinates and graph common polar curves including limacons, rose curves, lemniscates, and cardioids.
standards.ccssText: Convert between polar coordinates (r, theta) and rectangular coordinates (x, y) using x = r cos(theta) and y = r sin(theta); graph polar equations including circles, limacons, rose curves (r = a cos(n theta)), lemniscates, and cardioids; find intersections of polar curves.

standards.skillName: Area and Arc Length in Polar
standards.description: Teach students to set up and evaluate integrals for area enclosed by polar curves and arc length of polar curves.
standards.ccssText: Find the area enclosed by a polar curve using A = (1/2) integral(r^2 d theta); find the area between two polar curves; compute arc length using L = integral(sqrt(r^2 + (dr/d theta)^2) d theta); identify correct limits of integration from the graph.

standards.skillName: Vectors in the Plane and Space
standards.description: Help students define 2D and 3D vectors, perform operations including dot and cross products, and write equations of lines and planes in space.
standards.ccssText: Represent vectors in 2D and 3D in component and unit vector forms; perform vector addition, scalar multiplication, dot product, and cross product; find equations of lines (parametric and symmetric) and planes in 3D space; interpret dot and cross products geometrically.

standards.description: Help students define sequences and their limits, and determine convergence or divergence using limit laws and the Squeeze Theorem.
standards.ccssText: Define a sequence as a function whose domain is the positive integers; find the limit of a sequence using limit laws, L'Hopital's Rule, or the Squeeze Theorem; classify sequences as convergent or divergent, and as increasing, decreasing, or bounded.

standards.description: Guide students to define infinite series and partial sums and apply divergence, integral, comparison, limit comparison, ratio, and root tests.
standards.ccssText: Define an infinite series as the limit of its sequence of partial sums; apply the Divergence Test, Integral Test, Direct Comparison Test, Limit Comparison Test, Ratio Test, and Root Test to determine convergence or divergence of positive-term series.

standards.description: Teach students to apply the Alternating Series Test and distinguish between absolute and conditional convergence, and estimate error using the alternating series remainder.
standards.ccssText: Apply the Alternating Series Test to determine convergence of series with alternating signs; define absolute convergence (series of absolute values converges) and conditional convergence; estimate the error in a partial sum approximation using the alternating series remainder bound.

standards.description: Help students find the radius and interval of convergence of a power series and differentiate and integrate power series term by term.
standards.ccssText: Define a power series centered at x = a; use the Ratio Test to find the radius of convergence R; determine the interval of convergence by testing endpoints; differentiate and integrate power series term by term within the interval of convergence.

standards.description: Guide students to derive Taylor and Maclaurin series for standard functions and estimate error using the Lagrange remainder bound.
standards.ccssText: Derive the Taylor series for f centered at x = a using f(x) = sum[f^(n)(a)/n! * (x-a)^n]; know Maclaurin series for e^x, sin x, cos x, 1/(1-x), and ln(1+x); use the Lagrange error bound |R_n(x)| <= M|x-a|^(n+1)/(n+1)! to estimate the remainder.

standards.description: Teach students to apply the binomial series and use known series to derive new series and evaluate limits without L'Hopital's Rule.
standards.ccssText: Apply the binomial series (1+x)^k = sum[C(k,n) x^n] for |x| < 1; use known Taylor series to find series for related functions by substitution, differentiation, or integration; evaluate limits of the form (f(x)/g(x)) as x approaches 0 using series expansion.
